prompt:
Based on the comprehensive audit you just provided (39 issues), please give me clear, simple, actionable instructions on what to do first.

IMPORTANT: Please keep things simple and straightforward. Don't overcomplicate. I want to fix the most critical issues first, one group at a time.

Please tell me:
1. What is the very first thing I should fix? Give me specific, simple steps.
2. What are the next few things after that?
3. What should I prioritize?

Keep the instructions simple, practical, and easy to follow. Don't add unnecessary complexity — just tell me exactly what to fix and how, starting with the most important issues.
response:
Start with the Engineering Network. It is the first major section after the hero, and its disconnected nodes and barely visible connections are the most noticeable problems in the screenshot.

Don't try to fix all 39 issues at once. Work through the following groups in order, completing and verifying each before moving to the next.

1. FIRST: Fix the Engineering Network
Priority 1 — Fix first

Target: A connected engineering system with readable domain nodes and clearly visible signal paths.

What's wrong: The domain labels appear to float independently. The green signal line at the top does not visibly connect to the nodes below it.

What to do:

Open the Engineering Network in a real browser and check whether the connections become visible after the animation finishes.

If they remain disconnected, inspect the SVG connection paths and the actual positions of the nodes.

Correct the connection coordinates so every line starts and ends at its intended node.

Increase the visibility of the connection lines and node labels.

Make the selected node and its related connections clearly distinguishable.

Test the network at desktop and mobile widths, including after resizing the browser.

Done when: All eight domain nodes are readable, the intended connections align correctly, and selecting a node highlights its related connections.

Do not redesign the network or introduce new animation libraries. Fix the existing implementation.

2. NEXT: Fix the Home Security architecture
Priority 2 — Flagship project

What's wrong: Your most important project appears as a long, narrow column of tiny cards. The text and connecting lines are difficult to read, and the different subsystems look too similar.

What to do:

Make the architecture wider on desktop instead of keeping everything in a narrow central column.

Increase the size of the subsystem cards and their text.

Make the connecting lines clearly visible.

Use the existing signal colors and technical labels to distinguish sensors, communication, processing, and services.

Give the Raspberry Pi services branch enough space to show its individual connections.

Ensure the complete architecture remains understandable on mobile, using a vertical layout where necessary.

Done when: A visitor can follow the entire system from the sensor nodes to the mobile app and read the component names without zooming.

Keep the existing architecture and scroll interactions. This is a layout and readability correction, not a new project design.

3. THEN: Fix global readability and spacing
Priority 3 — Whole website

What's wrong: Small technical labels, weak contrast, inconsistent panel widths, and excessive empty space make the engineering demonstrations less effective.

What to do:

Increase the readability of important technical labels, descriptions, and numerical values.

Improve contrast between grey text, connection lines, and dark backgrounds.

Standardize the outer layout of the project demonstration sections.

Reduce unnecessary empty space where it makes the engineering content appear undersized.

Keep each demonstration's unique internal design rather than making every panel identical.

Done when: The sections feel consistent, important information is comfortably readable, and the engineering diagrams have appropriate visual prominence.

4. AFTER THAT: Polish the individual demonstrations
Priority 4 — Project interactions

Fix these one at a time, using the existing components.

Ultrasonic Tape Measure

Clearly identify the sensor and target, emphasize the distance reading, and clarify how to move the target.

Joystick ADC

Make the joystick more recognizable and improve the presentation of the ADC values and UART output.

FPGA Timing Diagram

Improve waveform readability, control labels, and the selected truth-table state. Verify that the displayed transitions are technically correct.

ARM Debugger

Make the active instruction, register values, and execution controls easier to read and distinguish.

Power Engineering

Enlarge the technical diagrams, improve their labels, and verify that the phase-angle slider updates all related measurements correctly.

5. LAST: Complete the homepage presentation
Priority 5 — Final polish

Once the main engineering sections are working and visually stable, address the remaining presentation issues.

Improve the hero composition, connect the global signal visually across the homepage, refine the Contact section, and ensure each project has a clear link to its detailed case study.

Add authentic project photos, technical evidence, and verified results where appropriate. Do not invent content just to fill empty space.
